postings.title: Accounting Manager, Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting
postings.text:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

Accounting Manager, Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting

San Francisco, CA (Hybrid)

About The Role

We are seeking a highly motivated Accounting Manager, Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting to play a key role in building and scaling Snorkel's accounting organization.

This position combines technical accounting expertise with operational excellence. You will partner closely with the Controller and Accounting team to own key areas of the monthly close, prepare technical accounting analyses, support financial statement audits, and help establish scalable accounting processes and internal controls.

The ideal candidate enjoys solving complex accounting issues while remaining hands-on in day-to-day accounting operations. You thrive in a fast-paced startup environment, embrace ambiguity, and enjoy building processes that support a rapidly scaling business.

What You'll Do

Month-End Close & General Accounting

• Support and help lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes.

• Prepare and review journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, and supporting schedules.

• Perform detailed balance sheet reconciliations and investigate reconciling items.

• Prepare monthly flux analyses and explain significant balance sheet and income statement variances.

• Ensure the integrity of the general ledger and compliance with U.S. GAAP.

• Assist in improving close processes with the goal of achieving a world-class close timeline.

Technical Accounting

• Research, document, and implement technical accounting guidance under U.S. GAAP.

• Prepare technical accounting memos supporting complex accounting conclusions.

• Partner with business leaders to evaluate accounting implications of new transactions and commercial arrangements.

• Maintain accounting policies and ensure consistent application across the organization.

Areas of ownership may include:

• ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

• ASC 842 Lease Accounting

• Stock-based Compensation (ASC 718)

• Equity transactions and equity rollforward

• Debt accounting and warrant accounting

• Business combinations and asset acquisitions, as applicable

• Significant estimates and management judgments

• Capitalized software and internal-use software accounting

• New accounting standard implementations

Financial Reporting

• Prepare financial statements and supporting schedules in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

• Support quarterly and annual financial reporting requirements.

• Prepare audit-ready workpapers and accounting schedules.

• Assist in preparing disclosures for financial statements.

• Develop standardized reporting packages for management and external stakeholders.

Audit & Internal Controls

• Serve as a primary accounting contact for external auditors.

• Coordinate audit requests and maintain organized supporting documentation.

• Prepare accounting position papers and respond to technical accounting inquiries from auditors.

• Support walkthroughs, testing, and implementation of internal controls.

• Assist with developing and documenting accounting policies, narratives, and process documentation.

Cross-Functional Partnership

• Partner with Finance, Legal, Revenue, People, and Operations to support new initiatives.

• Review customer contracts for accounting implications.

• Support equity issuances, financing activities, and strategic transactions.

• Assist with bonus accruals, commission accounting, and other compensation-related accounting.

• Participate in special projects, system implementations, and process improvement initiatives.

Process Improvement

• Identify opportunities to automate accounting processes and improve operational efficiency.

• Build scalable accounting processes capable of supporting a rapidly growing organization.

• Develop best practices around reconciliations, documentation, and financial reporting.

• Help strengthen the company's internal control environment.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting.

• CPA required or actively pursuing CPA.

• 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including public accounting and/or high-growth technology companies.

• Strong technical accounting knowledge under U.S. GAAP.

• Experience supporting financial statement audits.

• Experience preparing technical accounting memos and accounting policy documentation.

• Strong understanding of financial statement preparation and financial reporting.

• Experience supporting month-end close in a fast-paced environment.

• Advanced knowledge of Excel and Google Sheets.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities with exceptional attention to detail.

Preferred Qualifications

• Big Four or national public accounting experience.

• CPA license.

• Experience in a high-growth SaaS, AI, or technology company.

• Experience with project-based, milestone-based, or services revenue models.

• Strong understanding of ASC 606.

• Experience with ASC 842 lease accounting.

• Experience accounting for stock-based compensation under ASC 718.

• Experience with equity accounting, capitalization tables, and equity rollforwards.

• Experience accounting for debt instruments, warrants, and other complex financing transactions.

• Experience supporting annual financial statement audits.

• Experience designing and documenting internal controls.

• Experience implementing accounting systems or ERP solutions.

• Familiarity with Salesforce, QuickBooks, NetSuite, or similar financial systems.

Bonus Points For

• Experience building accounting functions in venture-backed startups.

• Experience with AI, cloud infrastructure, or professional services businesses.

• Experience with milestone or consumption-based revenue models.

• Experience with project accounting and percentage-of-completion or milestone billing environments.

• Experience preparing accounting white papers for auditors.

• Experience supporting due diligence for financing or M&A transactions.

Location

Bay Area required, 3x a week in-office hybrid schedule in downtown SF.

Be Your Best at Snorkel

Joining Snorkel AI means becoming part of a company that has market-proven solutions, robust funding, and is scaling rapidly, offering a unique combination of stability and the excitement of high growth. As a member of our team, you'll have meaningful opportunities to shape our accounting infrastructure, influence key accounting policies, and help build a world-class finance organization.

Whether you're looking to deepen your technical accounting expertise, lead strategic accounting initiatives, or help build scalable financial operations, you'll be supported in an environment designed for growth, learning, and shared success.

postings.title: Corporate FP&A Manager
postings.text:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

The Role

The Corporate FP&A Manager will own headcount and operating expense planning across Snorkel and serve as the finance partner to department leaders. You will turn hiring and spending plans into reliable forecasts, help teams make investment decisions and build better cost visibility. You will also manage Ramp and procurement workflows and implement planning tools as the business grows.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead annual department budgets and rolling forecasts for headcount and non-headcount expenses, aligning spending with company growth and profitability targets.

• Own the headcount and personnel cost model with People and Recruiting, reflecting hiring plans, attrition, compensation and benefits.

• Partner with department leaders on hiring and investment decisions, identifying cost savings and evaluating tradeoffs in growth, capacity and profitability.

• Partner with Accounting on month-end close, including expense accruals, and lead headcount and OpEx variance analysis against budget and forecast.

• Own SaaS and vendor spend tracking, the purchase order system and procurement approvals, working with Legal, IT and Accounting on purchases and renewals.

• Own and manage Ramp, including spend programs, company cards, approval workflows and expense policies, in partnership with Accounting.

• Implement and administer planning tools such as Pigment or Anaplan and improve data integrations, reporting and planning processes.

• Partner with the Senior FP&A Manager to prepare consolidated financial reporting, with clear commentary on spending trends and outlook for executive reviews and board materials.

About You

• 5+ years of FP&A or business finance experience, including direct ownership of headcount and operating expense planning in a growing technology company.

• Advanced Excel and Google Sheets skills and experience building models that connect hiring, vendor commitments and operating drivers to financial forecasts.

• Hands-on experience managing Ramp, including spend approvals, expense controls and reporting.

• Experience implementing and administering planning systems such as Pigment, Anaplan or similar platforms, including financial model design and data integrations.

• Strong understanding of expense accruals, cost allocation and financial statements, with a record of partnering effectively with Accounting.

• Ability to build relationships with department leaders, explain financial tradeoffs clearly and turn analysis into recommendations.

• Strong attention to detail and the ability to establish practical processes, improve data quality and follow through across multiple workstreams.

Experience with SaaS or AI businesses, IT, cloud or inference costs, and contractor or services delivery economics is a plus.

Why This Role

This role is an opportunity to build the cost planning and spend management foundation of a growing AI company. You will help leaders make better hiring and investment decisions and translate operational improvements into stronger financial performance.

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

Salary range(s) for this role

$125,000—$180,000 USD

As a member of our team, you’ll have meaningful opportunities to shape priorities and initiatives, influence key strategic decisions, and directly impact our ongoing success. Whether you’re looking to deepen your technical expertise, explore leadership opportunities, or learn new skills across multiple functions, you’re fully supported in building your career in an environment designed for growth, learning, and shared success.

postings.title: Finance Manager, DaaS
locations: New York, New York, United States
postings.text:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

About the role

Reporting to the Senior Director of Finance, the DaaS Finance Manager is a critical member of the Finance org and a dedicated finance partner to the DaaS business as we scale.

You will drive the financial insights that lead to better decisions: what we charge, what it costs to deliver, how much we need to deliver, and how it all rolls into revenue and ARR. The job is not just reporting numbers, but telling leadership what they mean and what to do about them.

You will partner closely with the operating teams (Sales, Delivery Ops and RevOps) and bring finance rigor to how we work: clear assumptions, consistent definitions, and models people trust. Success is measured by outcomes, not outputs: deals priced to target margin, staffing plans that match demand, and a forecast leadership has confidence in.

Key responsibilities

The work falls into three pillars, with the mix shifting through the quarter.

1. Revenue model and forecast (with RevOps)

• Maintain the DaaS revenue model: bookings, acceptance-based revenue and ARR by deal, with scenario cases for planning.

• Partner with RevOps on the weekly revenue and ARR forecast, and run the weekly forecast deck and summary for leadership.

• Reconcile the field's call (commit, forecast, best case) with a deal-by-deal finance view; quantify coverage, swing deals and risks.

• Track delivery pacing and acceptance against plan and identify execution risks.

• Build bridges and variance analysis (forecast vs actual, bookings to revenue) for quarterly and annual planning.

• Build the DaaS inputs to the annual operating plan and long-range plan: revenue, cost of delivery, margin and delivery headcount, with monthly actuals-vs-plan variance analysis.

• Partner with Accounting on revenue recognition inputs, COGS and margin actuals.

2. Delivery capacity model

• Run and maintain the delivery capacity model in partnership with Delivery Ops, covering utilization, project mix, headcount per project and cost to deliver.

• Reconcile the capacity plan with actual staffing data and explain variances in mix, productivity and headcount.

• Translate the bookings pipeline into staffing demand and flag hiring or Expert Contributor needs ahead of the quarter.

• Lead a regular capacity planning review with Delivery leadership.

3. Business insights, pricing and strategic projects

• Turn the data into decisions: surface trends in pricing, mix, margin and pacing that leadership has not asked about yet, with a clear recommendation.

• Deal economics: partner with Deal Desk, which owns pricing, as deals need finance input; review deal models and pricing templates for accuracy and margin, and recommend adjustments.

• Customer and product profitability: cost to deliver by customer, project and product, tied to revenue.

• Product economics: what it takes for each product to hit margin targets, and where to invest next.

• Find broken or slow processes and recommend and drive fixes that shorten cycle time and improve data quality.

• Automate what repeats: move recurring models from manual spreadsheets toward scalable, auditable tools.

• Support board and investor content for the DaaS business.

What success looks like

By month six this person runs the weekly forecast and capacity model with the senior leader reviewing rather than building, and Deal Desk and RevOps rely on them to check deal economics.

• First 30 days: Meets the team and learns the DaaS model end to end: pricing, capacity, revenue and ARR. Shadows Deal Desk reviews and the forecast call. Co-produces one weekly forecast deck.

• First 60 days: Runs the weekly forecast deck and summary. Reviews Deal Desk models and templates independently. Leads one monthly capacity review with Delivery Ops.

• First 90 days: Recommends at least one fix to a Deal Desk or RevOps pricing template. Reconciles the capacity model to weekly staffing data with a documented variance bridge. Delivers a first customer or product profitability view.

• First year: Forecast accuracy and pacing calls trusted by the exec team. Margin and capacity assumptions refreshed every quarter without fire drills. Recurring models automated.

Qualifications

We want a builder who is equally comfortable in a deal negotiation thread and a 30-tab model, ideally with experience in a services-heavy, usage-based or manufacturing business.

Must-haves

• 5–8 years in FP&A, product or business finance, deal desk, or strategic finance; at least 2 at a high-growth tech company.

• Hands-on ownership of a revenue forecast and a unit-economics or pricing model, not just review of one.

• Fluency in gross margin vs contribution margin, cost-to-serve, and how pricing, discounting and incentives flow into both.

• Experience with services or labor-based delivery economics: utilization, headcount per project, contractor mix.

• Expert spreadsheet modeling (Google Sheets / Excel) and working SQL; comfortable pulling from a CRM and a data warehouse.

• Clear, concise executive communication: can write a five-line summary leadership can act on.

• Comfort with ambiguity: makes a reasoned call with incomplete data, states the assumptions, and refines as facts arrive.

• Process mindset: spots friction, proposes a simpler way, and drives it to adoption rather than working around it.

• Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, engineering or a related field.

Nice-to-haves

• Experience in AI/ML, data services, a marketplace with reusable inventory (resale economics), services or manufacturing.

• Familiarity with ARR-style metrics and acceptance-based revenue recognition.

• Board or investor materials experience, including fundraise data rooms.

• Uses AI tools and light scripting (Python) to automate recurring analysis.

• Experience with BI tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau) or planning tools (e.g., Adaptive, Pigment).

• Background at a top consulting, banking or finance-rotation program.

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

Salary range(s) for this role

$130,000—$180,000 USD
